findings.title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates the connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status in the UI
findings.body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop on success. Unlike `disconnectMutation` in the same component (which invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`), it never refetches/invalidates the `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` query that supplies `cacheUpdatedAt`. `onSuccess` maps to the wrapper's optional `onChanged` prop, which many usages don't provide or which doesn't refetch this query. Result: after successfully deleting cached data, the dropdown keeps showing 'Cache Status / Last updated: ...' for the deleted cache until a full page refresh, and the delete action can be invoked again against already-deleted data. Add the same `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` (or a refetch) to the delete mutation's onSettled.

findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ignores expiresAt, so expired cache rows are reported as active cache
findings.body: The groupBy in `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` filters only on `credentialId` and takes `_max.updatedAt`, without any condition on `expiresAt >= now()`. CalendarCache rows are not deleted when they expire (`getCachedAvailability` filters by `expiresAt` at read time, but expired rows linger in the table). Consequence: the UI will show 'Cache Status: Last updated ...' and a 'Delete cached data' action for credentials whose cache is entirely expired and never served, misleading users about the state of the cache. Filter out expired rows (e.g. `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }`) in the where clause.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId is called with an empty data object; the updatedAt bump is purely implicit and fragile
findings.body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty `data` payload. The code comment says the intent is to 'Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt', but no field is set explicitly; the effect relies entirely on Prisma's implicit `@updatedAt` behavior on an empty update, which varies by Prisma version (some versions reject empty update data with a validation error, and if the model's column lacks `@updatedAt` this is a silent no-op). If it throws, it breaks `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache`, which is called from the `unwatchCalendar` flow after cache repopulation. Pass the intent explicitly (e.g. `data: { updatedAt: new Date() }`) and verify it works against the Prisma version in use.

findings.title: Cache timestamp formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of the user's locale
findings.body: The component calls `useLocale()` for all translated strings but formats `cacheUpdatedAt` with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`. Non-English users will see a mixed-language UI with US-style dates (MM/DD/YYYY), which is ambiguous in most of the world (e.g. 03/04/2025 reads as March 4 vs 3 April). Use the locale from `useLocale()` (falling back appropriately) as the first argument to `Intl.DateTimeFormat`.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId on selected calendars, tightening the contract for all callers
findings.body: The `UserWithCalendars` type's `allSelectedCalendars`/`userLevelSelectedCalendars` now `Pick` `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` from SelectedCalendar. Every caller that constructs this type must now select those columns (the PR already had to patch `findUnlockedUserForSession` in user.ts to compile), including external consumers such as platform-libraries that build users with selected calendars. Per the PR's own notes, `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is not even displayed in the frontend, so this widening forces extra DB columns to be selected on every session-user fetch for no consumer. If the fields aren't required by this feature, revert the type to avoid the breaking contract; if they are, verify all call sites (including platform packages) were updated.

findings.title: sed -i '' syntax is macOS-only and fails on GNU/Linux
findings.body: The script uses `sed -i '' -E "s|...|...|"` which is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU sed (standard on Linux CI/dev containers), the empty-string argument after `-i` is not treated as an in-place suffix, so sed interprets `''` as the script and the substitution expression as a filename, causing the command to fail with an error and leaving `.env` unmodified (or worse, running the wrong edit). Use a portable approach (e.g. `sed -i.bak` + remove the backup, or detect the OS), since this script is committed to the shared repo.

findings.title: Handler throws a plain Error instead of a TRPCError, producing an opaque 500 to clients
findings.body: `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` in a tRPC mutation surfaces as an unhandled INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR; in production the message may be stripped, and the client cannot distinguish 'not found' from 'unauthorized'. The rest of the codebase's tRPC handlers throw `TRPCError` with proper codes (e.g. `new TRPCError({ code: "UNAUTHORIZED" | "NOT_FOUND" })`). The client UI then only shows the generic 'error_deleting_cache' toast regardless of cause. Use TRPCError so the failure is properly coded and consistent with the surrounding routers.

findings.title: No tests for the new cache-status query, deleteCache handler, or the new UI component
findings.body: This PR adds a new repository method (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, including its groupBy/max semantics and how it interacts with expired rows), a new tRPC mutation (`deleteCache.handler`, including its ownership check), and a new interactive component (CredentialActionsDropdown with two destructive actions), but ships no unit or e2e tests for any of them. The PR description itself notes local end-to-end verification was not possible. At minimum, add unit tests for the credential-ownership/authorization path of deleteCacheHandler (e.g. a credential belonging to another user is rejected) and for getCacheStatusByCredentialIds, since these guard data deletion.
